events.title: The Battle of Montgisard
events.shortBlurb: On St. Catherine's day the leper-king Baldwin IV, with a handful of knights and the Templars, broke Saladin's host near Ramla…
body: In November 1177 much of the fighting strength of the Kingdom of Jerusalem had marched north toward Syria, and Saladin seized the moment to invade from Egypt toward the Holy City, letting his great army disperse to plunder Ramla and Lydda in confidence that no force could withstand him.

The sixteen-year-old King Baldwin IV, though already wasting under leprosy, mustered what men remained at Ascalon, joined by some eighty Knights Templar from Gaza under their master Odo of St Amand and a few hundred knights. On 25 November 1177, the feast of St. Catherine of Alexandria, he had the relic of the True Cross raised before the army and fell upon Saladin's scattered host at Montgisard, near Ramla, before it could form for battle.

The Muslim army was routed and pursued for miles; Saladin fled and reached Egypt on 8 December with but a tenth of his men. In thanksgiving a Benedictine priory dedicated to St. Catherine was built upon the field, and the victory bought the Crusader kingdom a decade's respite. The precise site, perhaps ancient Gezer, is debated.
